stemMd: Why does the author mention purchase records and interviews?

options.label: A
options.textMd: To prove that written sources should always be rejected.

options.label: B
options.textMd: To replace the question of maintenance with a question about wages.

options.label: C
options.textMd: To illustrate the use of additional evidence to test an uncertain interpretation.

options.label: D
options.textMd: To show that interviews have no limitations.

options.label: E
options.textMd: To announce that the factory will reopen.

explanationMd: The archivist looks beyond one biased source type. Comparing records and testimony can support or challenge the initial interpretation, though each source still needs criticism. The examples demonstrate triangulation rather than certainty from any one source.

distractorRationale.a: Purchase records are themselves written sources.
distractorRationale.b: The additional sources address the same maintenance question.
